html:
The National Dialogue Quartet was a group of four Tunisian bodies that brought the country's parties to a deal in 2013, when its move to democracy was close to collapse. They were the main trade union, the employers' federation, the human rights league and the bar association.

After the revolution, the Islamist party Ennahda led the government. In 2013 two left-wing politicians were murdered, and mass protests demanded its fall. The Quartet brokered a deal: Ennahda handed power to a caretaker government, and parliament finished a new constitution in January 2014. Elections followed.

The Quartet won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2015. Its success is why Tunisia was long called the one success of the Arab Spring.
